A few years ago, I was at a friend's house to help set up an outdoor movie night. I was in charge of hanging the tarp that would serve as our makeshift screen. It was a warm summer evening, and the sky was filled with stars. As I began to lift the tarp and position it against the wall, I misjudged the angle and the tarp slipped from my grip, tearing a small hole near the corner. 

My heart sank as I quickly tried to assess the damage. I had been so focused on getting everything perfect, and this small flaw was a stark reminder of how easy it was to slip up. My friend looked at me with concern and asked if I was okay.

In that moment, I realized that no matter how careful or prepared we are, mistakes are an inevitable part of the process. The tarp, far from being ruined, actually added character to the setup - it made the screen feel more lived-in, like it had survived a few screenings already.
